annotation.title_clean: Regulations Amending the Canadian Aviation Regulations (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems): SOR/2019-11
annotation.title_en: Regulations Amending the Canadian Aviation Regulations (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems): SOR/2019-11
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Governor General in Council, on recommendation of the Minister of Transport (Transport Canada)
annotation.venue: Canada Gazette, Part II, Vol. 153, No. 1
annotation.summary_en: Canadian regulations adding Part IX to the Canadian Aviation Regulations for drones of 250 g to 25 kg. They set drone registration, pilot certification (basic and advanced), operating rules, manufacturer safety declarations, and special flight operations certificates. The accompanying impact analysis shows a net monetized cost of $28.4M and aims to improve safety and predictability for operators.
key_provisions_or_claims: All drones 250 g–25 kg must be registered and display a registration number
Pilots need basic or advanced certificates (min. age 14/16) with 24-month recency
Operations in controlled airspace, near people, or near airports require advanced certification and a manufacturer self-declaration to Standard 922
Operations beyond line of sight, over 400 ft, at events, or with hazardous payloads need a Special Flight Operations Certificate
Autonomous systems where pilot cannot take immediate control are prohibited
